March 2010 # **15****th** **March – 26****th** **March** # **Spot premium for import cathode continues to decline** The spot premium for imported cathode saw a declining trend since the end of January 2010, with the spot premium quotation now in the range of $60- 100/t. Meanwhile, the premium for imported SXEW cathode is quoted at $60-70/t. Traders report that the import cathode spot market seems weaker recently. Downstream consumers’ buying interest is weak and very few deals have been closed. Usually the spot premium for imported cathode is a good indicator of market sentiment. There are three drivers for the gloomy imported cathode spot market at the moment. Firstly, there is no rapid improvement in consumption yet. At the same time, domestic supply is abundant given that domestic cathode output and imported cathode remain at high levels. The most important point is that the SHFE stock and off-warrant stocks are at high levels compared to 2009. Chinese customs will adjust the customs regulations on scrap starting from April 1st 2010. The adjustment is aimed improving the regulation of the copper scrap imports process to ensure that import value added tax on the full content of copper is being paid. This stipulation gives a more exact definition to the name and description of copper scrap. We believe that this may increase import costs and tighten scrap supply to some extent. Correspondingly, it may boost cathode demand as replacement of scrap. Bearing in mind the negative impact that the Chinese customs crack down on scrap copper imports had on scrap supply last year, we will wait for the scrap import data – to be released in May - to find out what the real impact has been on scrap supply. # **Air conditioner energy efficiency ratio to be raised** The State Administr

ation of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine and National Standardization Management Committee have announced that a new room air conditioner energy efficiency limit and energy efficiency ratio grade will be effective starting from 1st June 2010. According to the announcement, the energy efficiency limit will be raised by 23%. At present, the main - and easiest - way for certain air conditioners to increase the air conditioner energy efficiency ratio is to adopt a high active compressor and increase the size of the evaporator coil and condenser. It may increase raw materials (including copper tube) usage for air conditioners while raising the production cost, though this will not apply negative pressure to sales of air conditioners due to the fiscal subsidy program for energy efficient appliances. We believe air conditioner producers may try to find other methods to realise higher energy efficiency without increasing costs, such as by adopting more advanced technology and ensuring that appropriate sizes of air conditioning units are installed in specific areas. However, we note that average copper unit consumption in air conditioner has seen a decline in recent years, mainly driven by the promotion of direct frequency conversion technology and moves to make system pipelines smaller with thinner tube diameters. Therefore, it seems too early to say whether the adjustment of air conditioner energy efficiency standards is good news for copper consumption. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 3 **March 2010** www.crumonitor.com # **Strong Chinese seasonal demand – a little too optimistic?** SHFE 3-month price seems sluggish

The LME 3-month copper price fluctuated between $7300/t to $7500/t in the last two weeks. Although Eurozone debt issues and Chinese inflation worries have brought downward pressure on copper prices, estimates from some quarters of strong Chinese seasonal demand would support the view that the copper price will remain at high levels. However, the SHFE market seems sluggish, with no sign of a demand rally approaching. In the last two weeks the SHFE 3-month copper price ranged from RMB58,000/t to RMB59,000/t, and the SHFE/LME 3-month average price ratio declined to 7.89, compared to 7.94. We do hear from market insiders that Chinese demand may improve in Q2, but we are inclined not to cherish too much hope that strong Chinese seasonal demand may drive a surge in the copper price. Chinese copper market stocks (including SHFE and off-warrant stocks) are at high levels compared to early 2009, and so pressure from the stocks may offset demand improvement to some extent. We believe that a bullish view of the copper price needs to be based on fundamental improvement instead of just hope

s of a demand rally. We see further fundamental improvements in April, but for the next two weeks we forecast that the copper price will continue to fluctuate below $7,600/t.
